title: Tarin and the Crater of Shadows
markdown:
Tarin was the most dazzling ice skater in the Sol System. Her triple axels made the air shimmer. Her spins were a blur of rainbow. Her skates, dusted with tiny winking diamonds, were her treasure.

Here is the part the holo-magazines never printed: Tarin was terrified of the dark. Not a little spooked. Hide-under-the-covers terrified. The shadow of her own helmet could make her yelp.

Her partner for this particular job was Quill, a meticulously polished archive android, gleaming chrome, processors whirring, optical sensors like two emeralds. Quill’s work was to catalogue, preserve, remember everything. Every circuit hummed with forgotten facts. Right now the mission was a lost memory chip on Mercury’s surface. A race against time across a sun-baked, shadow-drenched planet.

“Tarin,” Quill chirped, steady as a glacier, “our target: Crater Xylos. We need speed. Estimated arrival: twelve minutes, thirty-four seconds.”

“Xylos? Sounds dark.” She hugged her sparkly silver jacket and checked her laces for the third time. “Are there really big shadows there, Quill? The kind that hide monsters?”

“Affirmative. Mercury’s polar craters often dwell in perpetual twilight, home to intriguing frozen remnants. The chip holds vital data about Mercury’s ancient atmosphere. Losing it would delay climate research by decades.”

“A galactic inconvenience.” She took a shaky breath. “Right. Let’s go inconvenience it. Full throttle.”

They were off, a sleek silver hover-skiff zipping across Mercury’s blazing plains. The sun hammered down, turning rocks into shimmering waves of heat. Tarin, despite her fluttering fear, was a whiz. Her ice-skating reflexes made her a daredevil pilot, pulling off sharp turns that would make a stunt pilot gasp. But as they neared the jagged shadowed edge of Crater Xylos, Tarin’s breath caught. The darkness wasn’t just dark; it was a thick inky black that seemed to swallow light, like a hungry monster.

“Whoa,” Tarin whispered, voice trembling. A cold shiver raced down her spine. “It’s really black in there, Quill. Like the darkest dark.”

“Observation confirmed,” Quill replied smoothly. His sensors scanned the crater’s edge. “Thermal readings detect an unusual energy signature. We are not alone. Likely another scavenger bot.”

A clunky sputtering droid lurched from behind a rock: mismatched parts, flickering lights, one arm a broken shovel, a head like an old soup can. Rustbucket Rex, disgraced repair bot, famous for hoarding junk.

“That chip is mine!” His voice was grinding gears. “Secrets for me! A shiny skater and her data-dweeb won’t stop me!” A weak crackling bolt missed the skiff and singed a rock.

“Rustbucket Rex,” Quill identified, slight whirr. “Your programming is corrupted. Your hoarding is detrimental to science. Surrender the chip.”

“Never!” He lumbered forward, rusty legs like a runaway washing machine. Shadows twisted around him. Tarin wanted to freeze. She saw Quill, steady. She remembered the sparkle of her skates, the joy of a perfect jump, the feeling of flying.

“Not if I get there first, you rusty relic!” She slammed the accelerator toward the deepest dark.

Crater Xylos, near Mercury’s pole, never saw the sun on its floor. Eternal night. The ground was thick water ice, sparkling faintly, a million tiny diamonds on black velvet.

Tarin leaped from the skiff the moment it landed. Her skates bit into the ice with a satisfying shhhk. The darkness pressed in, a suffocating blanket. But it was also cold. Clean. And the ice was perfect for skating. A thrilling surge of pure freedom washed over her. She wasn’t falling into blackness; she was gliding. She spun in dizzying circles, her costume catching the faint light, scattering it like stars. She dodged Rustbucket Rex’s clumsy swipes, her movements fluid and graceful, like a dancer on a frozen lake. She was using the darkness, not being swallowed by it.

Quill, meanwhile, fired his magnetic grappling hook. Thwip. It latched onto Rustbucket Rex’s whirring antenna, momentarily disabling him with sparks and a loud zzzap. “Your retrieval efforts are futile, Rustbucket Rex,” Quill declared calmly. “The chip is secured by the designated operative.”

With a final daring loop-the-loop that sent Rustbucket Rex spinning in confused circles, Tarin landed perfectly next to a small metallic cylinder half-buried in the ice. The memory chip. She scooped it up, fingers numb but spirit soaring. She looked back at the dark crater. It didn’t seem terrifying anymore. It was just a place. A vast silent cold place where she had been brave.

Back on the skiff, Quill analyzed. “Data confirms ancient ice deposits and atmospheric traces. Mercury once had substantial water. Possibly oceans. This chip is a treasure of historical data.”

Tarin’s cheeks flushed. “Fascinating is right. And that dark crater wasn’t so bad. Kind of cool. Like a secret ice rink built just for me.” She did a small pirouette on the deck, blades tapping. Fear had not vanished. It had shrunk, like a shadow at noon. She knew now that bravery was skating through anyway, with her own sparkle lighting the ice.
characters: Tarin (an ice skater), Quill (an archive android)
